Traditional Polish Christmas Eve Pierogi

Served at: Christmas Eve

Serves 6Prep 45 minCook 20 min

Pierogi are classic Polish dumplings filled with various savory or sweet fillings. On Christmas Eve, pierogi with mushroom and sauerkraut filling are a beloved dish symbolizing the festive spirit and family togetherness during Wigilia, the traditional Polish Christmas Eve dinner.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (375 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 large egg
  • 1 cup (240 ml) warm water
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) unsalted butter, melted
  • 2 cups (300 g) sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
  • 1 1/2 cups (200 g) dried mushrooms
  • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • 2 tablespoons (30 ml) vegetable oil
  • Salt and pepper to taste
  • Optional: sour cream for serving

Method

  1. Soak dried mushrooms in warm water for 30 minutes, then drain and chop finely, reserving some soaking liquid.
  2. In a pan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat and sauté the chopped onion until translucent.
  3. Add chopped mushrooms and sauerkraut to the pan, cooking for about 10 minutes until flavors meld. Season with salt and pepper, then set aside to cool.
  4. In a large bowl, combine flour and salt. Make a well in the center and add egg, warm water, and melted butter.
  5. Mix and knead the dough on a floured surface until smooth and elastic, about 8-10 minutes. Cover and let rest for 30 minutes.
  6. Roll out the dough to about 1/8 inch (3 mm) thickness. Cut into 3-inch (7.5 cm) circles using a cutter or glass.
  7. Place a teaspoon of filling in the center of each circle. Fold dough over to form a half-moon shape and press edges firmly to seal.
  8. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Drop pierogi in batches and cook until they float to the surface plus 2 more minutes.
  9. Remove with a slotted spoon and optionally sauté in butter until golden before serving.
  10. Serve warm with sour cream if desired.

Tips

  • Use fresh mushrooms if available for a more intense flavor.
  • Pierogi dough can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 24 hours.
  • For a sweeter Christmas variation, try pierogi filled with sweetened farmer's cheese and raisins.
